title: Bill Cassidy Will Back Todd Blanche as Attorney General, Salvaging His Confirmation
partialText: The Louisiana senator said that, despite reservations,  he would back President Trump’s pick for attorney general, giving Republicans enough votes for a majority.

title: Prosecutor Sues Justice Dept. Over Dismissal After Right-Wing Influencer’s Claim
partialText: Will Rosenzweig joins a growing list of former prosecutors and federal agents who have gone to court to contest the purge of law enforcement deemed disloyal.

title: Weak Jobs Report Does Not Eliminate Prospects of Interest Rate Rise
partialText: Officials at the Federal Reserve are chiefly focused on the trajectory of inflation after five years of overshooting the central bank’s 2 percent target.

title: The Bond Market Is Signaling Rising Risks. Investors Should Listen.
partialText: While the Fed didn’t raise rates, the bond market did. That means hardship for home buyers and higher hurdles for A.I. data centers and the stock market. But it’s also a boon for retirees.

title: Abdul El-Sayed Talks About His Victory, Chuck Schumer and His Mom
partialText: In an interview with The New York Times, Dr. El-Sayed recalled some of his conversations with establishment figures who once opposed his candidacy.

title: Candidate Field Set After Republicans Redrew Tennessee District Lines
partialText: Tennessee’s primary elections on Thursday came after Republican legislators carved up the state’s only majority-Black district in a bid to win all nine of the state’s House seats.

title: Seized on Their Way to Gaza, Activists Tell of Abuse in Israeli Custody
partialText: In interviews, more than 20 people who tried to break an Israeli blockade described beatings, electric shocks and other abuse after being captured. Israel denied the accusations.

title: The State of Iran’s Three Key Nuclear Sites
partialText: The conflict may have slowed, but not stopped, Iran’s nuclear program, officials and experts said.

title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan Sign Joint Defense Pact
partialText: The agreement treats an attack on any of the countries as an attack on all, but in a region of volatile rivalries, it was unclear how it would work in practice.

title: Pope Leo XIV Was Elected. The Chicago White Sox Were Resurrected.
partialText: The elevation of Pope Leo XIV, a Chicago native and lifelong supporter of the Sox, was a godsend for a team failing on the field and with fans.

title: An ICE Detention Center Roils a Colorado Town and Jolts a House Race
partialText: Tiny Hudson, Colo., was mostly known as a speed trap between plains and suburbs. Then ICE announced it was coming, setting off months of protests.

title: Voter-Registration Error Could Cost Immigrants a Shot at a Green Card
partialText: New Jersey improperly added as many as 6,600 noncitizens to its voter rolls. Those people could now be forced out of the country.

title: Twin Falls Embraces Man Who Confronted Idaho In-N-Out Shooting
partialText: While the motive in the strip mall shooting rampage in Twin Falls, Idaho, remains elusive, a community embraces a bystander who stepped in.

title: Drought and Aging Pipes Plunge Puerto Rico Into Another Water Crisis
partialText: Starting on Friday, the island’s water authority is scheduled to shut off water for rotating 48-hour periods in parts of San Juan and surrounding areas.

title: Trump Administration Fast-Tracks Military Partnership With Colombia to Target Drug Traffickers
partialText: The country’s new Trump-endorsed president takes office on Friday. Sweeping plans to target drug traffickers with U.S. help are already underway.

title: A Drying Danube River Reveals Nazi-Era Vessels, and Hazards of Heat
partialText: The river’s water levels have fallen as extreme heat has afflicted Europe, exposing sunken German vessels from World War II that are impeding navigation.

title: Photos Show England Turning Brown in Drought
partialText: Beset by historically dry weather, much of the nation is losing its signature hue.

title: Parts of Eastern and Central Europe Broke Heat Records This Week
partialText: The hot weather has exacerbated dry conditions, creating conditions for wildfires and receding rivers.

title: Boy Kills Grandparents and Then Five Teachers, Thai Authorities Say
partialText: A student killed his grandparents before opening fire at his high school and shooting himself, the authorities said. The episode revived a debate about gun laws.

title: Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner on Rom-Coms and the Politics of ‘One Night Only’
partialText: In “One Night Only,” Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner play singles living in a world where the government has banned premarital sex. How far-fetched is that?

title: ‘One Night Only’ Review: A 12-Hour Sexual Reprieve
partialText: This dystopian rom-com follows Allie (Monica Barbaro) and Owen (Callum Turner), on their parallel hunts for passion.

title: A Generation on Antidepressants Searches for the Exit
partialText: Many people feel that antidepressants block their true emotions, but they don’t have guidance about how to get off these drugs.

title: ‘The First Time I Voted for Donald Trump, I Thought It Was Going to Make a Difference’
partialText: In Georgia, where Black voters could help decide control of the Senate, Mara Gay asks what they want from America and the Democratic Party.

title: Curious Minds
partialText: We’re answering reader questions.

title: Luigi Mangione Is Facing Two Trials. Isn’t That Double Jeopardy?
partialText: The legal principle prevents a person from being tried twice for the same crime. But Mr. Mangione’s situation shows how complicated the judicial system can be.
